links.outcome: Agreement of AI HAI surveillance with manual point prevalence survey on local patients
links.effect: Among 749 patients, PPS found 61 patients with 65 HAI; HAIDI found 62 patients with 65 HAI; Cohen's kappa 0.8849, observed agreement 0.9826; detection proportion 90.3% for both.
links.quote: Agreement between the two approaches was high (Cohen's kappa κ = 0.8849; observed agreement 0.9826).

links.outcome: AI surveillance performance compared against manual standard-of-care PPS on same cohort
links.effect: HAIDI and manual PPS each detected 90.3% of combined infections and both missed seven HAI, though different ones; kappa 0.8849.
links.quote: The detection proportion against the combined set of infections identified by either method was 90.3% for both manual PPS and HAIDI.

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic performance and concordance of an AI-assisted HAI surveillance system (HAIDI) deployed in routine practice compared to a standard point prevalence survey, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard variation.
